citations.authors: Ayaz M, Pasha MF, Alzahrani MY, Budiarto R, Stiawan D
citations.title: Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) as a meta standard for healthcare interoperability: systematic review
citations.what_it_says: Establishes FHIR as the dominant emerging interop standard, validating market demand for engineers and analysts who can implement FHIR resources and APIs.

citations.authors: Vorisek CN, Lehne M, Klopfenstein SAI, Mayer PJ, Bartschke A, Haese T, Thun S
citations.title: The evolution of the HL7 FHIR standard and its adoption in healthcare
citations.what_it_says: Documents rapid FHIR adoption across EHR vendors and payers following CMS interoperability rules, signaling rising demand for FHIR-credentialed integration talent.

citations.authors: Office of the National Coordinator for Health IT
citations.title: ONC Cures Act Final Rule: API certification criterion using FHIR Release 4
citations.what_it_says: Mandates FHIR R4 APIs for certified EHRs, creating federally enforced demand for FHIR-proficient developers at Epic, Oracle Health, athenahealth, and payers.

citations.title: 2023 HIMSS Health Informatics Workforce Survey
citations.what_it_says: Reports interoperability and FHIR-related roles among the fastest-growing informatics job categories, with salary premiums for credentialed interop specialists.

citations.title: HL7 FHIR Foundation and Proficiency certification program overview
citations.what_it_says: Per HL7 International's own program documentation (the standards body that authors and administers the credential), the FHIR Proficiency exam is offered as a low-cost, self-study assessment intended to signal baseline competency without requiring vendor sponsorship. Figures reflect HL7's published fee schedule at time of citation and should be re-verified against HL7's current program page.

citations.authors: Sengstack P, Boicey C, et al.
citations.title: Clinician informaticists and the bridge from practice to health IT industry roles
citations.what_it_says: Finds clinicians who add technical interop credentials transition successfully into vendor and payer informatics roles, though deeper engineering skills are often still required.
